chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen. A horse of a man from the people of Yemen escaped, and it passed galloping by a man, and kicked him with its foot, so it killed him. So the guardians of the killed man went to the owner and seized him, and brought him to Ali (peace be upon him). So the owner of the horse established the evidence in the presence of Ali (peace be upon him) that his horse had escaped from his house and kicked the man. So Ali (peace be upon him) invalidated the blood money (diyah) for their companion.

So the guardians of the killed man came from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Ali (peace be upon him) has been unjust to us and invalidated our companion.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) is not unjust, and he was not created for injustice. Verily, the Wilayah is for Ali (peace be upon him) after me, and the judgment is his judgment, and the word is his word. And none would repudiate his Wilayah, and his word, and his judgment except an infidel; and none would be pleased with his Wilayah, and his word, and his judgment except a believer.'

So when the Yemenis heard the word of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him), they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! We are pleased with the judgment of Ali (peace be upon him) and his word.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'It is your repentance from what you had said.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ: Guardians of the killed man (usually close male relatives)
key_terms.نَفَحَهُ: He kicked him (specifically with the hind leg)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on liability for damage caused by an animal in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *al-gharamah bi al-daman* (liability for damage) in early Islamic jurisprudence, where Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that an escaped horse causing death did not incur blood money from its owner, a decision the Prophet (peace be upon him) validated as authoritative. The Prophet’s declaration that 'his judgment is his judgment' underscores the concept of *Ismah* (infallibility) and the binding nature of Ali’s judicial rulings, linking legal correctness directly to his *Wilayah*. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for the Shia view that the Imam’s legal decisions are divinely guided and not subject to error.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ubeydullah Al Halby, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> sent Ali<sup>asws</sup> to Al-Yemen. A horse of a man from the people of Al-Yemen had escaped, and it had passed galloping by a man, and kicked him with its feed, so it had killed him. So the guardians of the killed one went over to the man and seized him, and brought him to Ali<sup>asws</sup>. So the owner of the horse established the evidence in the presence of Ali<sup>asws</sup> that his horse had escaped from his house and kicked the man’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> invalidated the blood (compensation) of their companion.

So the guardians of the killed one came over from Al-Yemen, to Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup>! Ali<sup>asws</sup> has been unjust to us and invalidated (the wergild) of our companion’. So Radool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> is not with injustice and had not been Created for the injustice. Verily, the Wilayah is for Ali<sup>asws</sup> from after me<sup>saww</sup>, and the (final) judgement is his<sup>asws</sup> judgement, and the (final) words are his<sup>asws</sup> words, and none would repudiate (deny) his<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, and his<sup>asws</sup> words, and his<sup>asws</sup> judgement except for an Infidel; and none would be pleased with his<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, and his<sup>asws</sup> words, and his<sup>asws</sup> judgements except for a Believer’.

So when the Yemenis heard the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> regarding Ali<sup>asws</sup>, they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We are pleased with the judgement of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and his<sup>asws</sup> words’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is your repentance from what you had said’.
